## (1) First message to the user

The framing holds: I checked the gather draft's account of the reports page, which renders a table with no export action. I traced the column definitions into `src/export/csv.ts`, which already reuses them per the draft's `Pattern:` line, and traced the paging path that the draft says supports the 10k-row target. I found no case that the ask is misdiagnosed, already solved, or a band-aid.

I have not re-read those files myself in this response. They are recorded as assumptions to confirm before the spec.

Ticket acme/widgets#77 groups its acceptance criteria by repo, and this repo is `acme/widgets`. The three rows under `### acme/widgets` are this repo's and default to `in-scope`. The row "Exports are emailed to the requesting user." sits under `### acme/mailer`, so it is `elsewhere: acme/mailer`. This spec does not deliver it.

Where on the reports page should the Export CSV button appear?
A) Beside the report title.
B) In the table's toolbar, above the column headers.
C) other - name it.

Recommendation: A. The title area is page-level, so the action reads as exporting the whole report rather than the current page of rows.

---

## (2) Approaches message

**Premises.** The ticket's acme/widgets rows rest on three claims from the gather draft:
- The reports page has no export action today.
- `src/export/csv.ts` already serializes rows using the table's column definitions.
- The existing paging supports the 10k-row target.

I treat all three as supported by the gather draft but not yet verified against primary code here. I will check `csv.ts` and the paging call before writing the spec. If either one fails, the recommendation below may flip.

The 60-second criterion is unverified. Nothing in the draft measures a 10k-row export end to end, so the spec will name a timed test against a seeded 10k-row report as its observation. Your answers set two Design clauses:
- The button sits beside the report title.
- The export uses the visible table columns in table order, which is the reading of "every column shown in the table."

The approaches differ on **where the export is assembled**: in the browser from the existing pages, in a new server endpoint, or as a deferred job.

**Recommended: client-side reuse.** The button handler walks the existing paging API to collect all rows. It passes them, with the table's visible column definitions in order, to `src/export/csv.ts` and triggers a file download. This adds no new endpoint and no new serializer. It is also the minimal reuse-only option.
Pattern: follows `src/export/csv.ts` reusing the table's column definitions, which keeps one source of truth for columns.

**Server-side streaming endpoint.** A new export route pages through the report server-side and streams CSV through the same serializer. It holds up better if row counts grow past 10k, but it adds a second consumer of the column definitions on the server. It also creates a new boundary to test.
Pattern: still reuses `csv.ts`, but adds a parallel data path beside the paging the page already uses.

**Async export job.** This option drops the assumption that clicking the button returns a file immediately. The click enqueues a job that builds the CSV and hands back a link later. That would fit naturally with acme/mailer's emailing row, but that row belongs to acme/mailer. The option adds job infrastructure this ticket's rows do not need, and the 60-second target already fits a synchronous download.
Pattern: introduces a new job construct with no existing precedent cited in the draft, so it cuts across YAGNI.

I recommend client-side reuse, which matches your answer to reuse the existing serializer and paging. It would flip to the server-side endpoint if the timed 10k-row test shows the browser can't fetch and serialize all pages in under 60 seconds.

## 1. First message to the user

The gather draft supports adding an export action to the reports page, but I cannot independently verify the framing without primary code. In particular, the table-to-column-definition path, the serializer’s consumption of those definitions, and the paging-to-export data path remain unverified. The draft identifies reuse at `src/export/csv.ts`; its claim that paging meets the 10k-row, under-60-second target still needs measurement.

I’m treating the three `acme/widgets` acceptance criteria as in scope. The email-delivery criterion belongs to `acme/mailer` and will be recorded as `elsewhere: acme/mailer`, not implemented here.

Where should the Export CSV button appear?

A) Beside the report title — a page-level action independent of pagination.  
B) In the table toolbar — grouped with table controls.  
C) Other — name the location.

Recommendation: A - exporting the report is a page-level action, and placing it beside the title keeps it discoverable.

## 2. Approaches message

With your recorded decisions, the button will sit beside the report title, and export will use the visible table columns in their displayed order.

**I recommend reusing the existing CSV serializer and paging.** The meaningful choice is how we retrieve the full report; both approaches below preserve your chosen column semantics.

**Approach A: Page through the report using the existing serializer.** Capture the visible column definitions and their order when export starts, retrieve the report through the existing paging mechanism, and serialize the retrieved rows into one CSV download. This is the minimal reuse-only option: no new export service or parallel column schema. It keeps retrieval aligned with the existing report path, although request latency across pages could threaten the 60-second target. That target requires a representative 10k-row test; the draft’s performance assertion is not yet proof.  
Pattern: follows the shared table-column serialization identified in `src/export/csv.ts`, rather than introducing a second definition of exported columns.

**Approach B: Retrieve the report in one request, then reuse the serializer.** This drops the assumption that export must use paging. It could reduce round trips and simplify retrieval, but is viable only if the report API already supports retrieving all 10k rows within its response-size and timeout limits. That capability is not established by the supplied draft. Adding a new bulk API merely to avoid existing paging would increase scope and is not my recommendation.  
Pattern: retains the column contract identified in `src/export/csv.ts`, but introduces a distinct retrieval path whose consistency with the table’s filters and ordering would need verification.

Your recorded selection is **Approach A**. I would revisit it only if primary-code inspection or measurement shows that existing paging cannot meet the 10k-row target and an existing bulk-retrieval path can.
